decision_conditions: The development hereby permitted shall be completed before the expiration of six months from the date of this permission.
REASON
To comply with Section 91 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.
The development hereby permitted shall not be carried out except in complete accordance with the details shown on the submitted plans, numbers:
REASON
To ensure the development complies with the provisions of the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 1 (2012) and Part 2 (2020), and the London Plan (2021).
For the lifetime of the development hereby permitted, the rating level (LAr) of noise caused by its operation shall not exceed:

55 dB LAr 1 hour for any one-hour period between 0700 and 2300, determined one-metre free field external to any window or door of any commercial premises, in accordance with 'Methods for rating and assessing industrial and commercial sound' British Standards Institution BS 4142:2014.'
REASON
To ensure those working inside would not be exposed to undue noise in accordance with Policies D13 and D14 of The London Plan (2021).

For the lifetime of the development hereby permitted, the noise level caused by structure-borne noise from the permitted development shall not exceed 40 dB LASMax at any time measured inside any room of any adjoining commercial premises.
REASON

To ensure that occupants of commercial premises are not unduly affected by structure-borne noise from the development in accordance with Policies D13 and D14 of The London Plan (2021) and with regard to 'Guide to evaluation of human exposure to vibration in buildings - Vibration sources other than blasting' British Standard 6472-1: 2008.

The final exit points of any kitchen extract system shall be positioned at least one metre above building roof level and discharged vertically upwards through high velocity cowls. These shall be installed before the expiration of six months from the date of this permission. Thereafter, the kitchen extract system shall be permanently maintained and retained as such.
REASON

To mitigate potential odour impacts in accordance with Policies D13 and D14 of the London Plan (2021) and Policy DMHB 11 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two - Development Management Policies (2020).

At least six cycle parking spaces shall be installed on site in accordance with Transport Statement, reference VP/JN/AT/AH/ITL18484-002a, prepared by i-Transport, dated 07.03.2024 and available for use in accordance with approved details and the London Cycle Design Standards within six months of the date of permission. The cycle parking spaces shall thereafter be permanently retained on site, maintained, and be kept available for use.
REASON

To ensure appropriate cycle parking provision in accordance with Policy T5 of The London Plan (2021) and Policies DMT 2 and DMT 5 of Hillingdon Council's Local Plan Part 2 Development Management Policies (2020).

An Operational Waste Management Strategy shall be submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority within three months of the date of permission. The approved Operational Waste Management Strategy shall thereafter be adhered to for the lifetime of the development unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
REASON
To ensure appropriate management of waste in accordance with Policy D6 of The London Plan (2021).

Within three months of the date of this permission, an Operational Management Plan (OMP) shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The OMP shall set out detailed measures for the day-to-day management and operation of the premises, with particular regard to the control of delivery operations, servicing, and driver behaviour associated with the use.
The OMP shall include, but not be limited to, the following details:

a) A schedule of delivery and collection times (including peak and off-peak hours) designed to minimise conflict with other occupiers of the Strategic Industrial Location and to reduce impacts on the local highway network and residential amenity;
b) Details of how delivery demand will be managed, including order batching, scheduling systems, and any limits on the number of concurrent deliveries;
c) Measures to ensure that delivery drivers do not park, idle, or congregate on surrounding roads, footways, or other unauthorised areas, inc
No deliveries from the premises to customers shall take place outside the hours of 0800 and 0100 hours daily.
REASON

To safeguard the amenity of the surrounding area and nearby occupiers, and to minimise noise and disturbance arising from delivery operations, in accordance with Policy D14 of The London Plan (2021) and Policies DMHB 11, DME 2, and DMEI 14 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part 2 - Development Management Policies (2020).

In dealing with the application the Council has implemented the requirement in the National Planning Policy Framework to work with the applicant in a positive and proactive way. We have made available detailed advice in the form of our statutory policies from Local Plan Part 1, Local Plan Part 2, Supplementary Planning Documents, Planning Briefs and other informal written guidance, as well as offering a full pre-application advice service, in order to ensure that the applicant has been given every opportunity to submit an application which is likely to be considered favourably.

It is considered that a condition based on fixed noise levels is consistent with noise and planning policy by relating external noise levels to the point at which adverse effects on health and quality of life start to be observed. The limit values are intended to be consistent with the evidence base that is reflected in guidance: 'Guidance on Sound Insulation and Noise Reduction for Buildings' BS 8233:2014. This is combined with the assessment principles and procedures detailed in guidance: 'Methods for rating and assessing industrial and commercial sound' British Standards Institution BS 4142:2014. This is used to set reference time periods for the assessment and adjust measured or calculated LAeq values for character as detailed in BS 4142:2014 to determine the rating level.

The applicant is advised that the flue and extraction system shall be installed and maintained in accordance with recognised best practice, including the DEFRA Guidance on the Control of Odour and Noise from Commercial Kitchen Exhaust Systems (2022) or any subsequent update. The system shall be regularly cleaned and kept in good working order to prevent odour or emissions affecting neighbouring units.
description: Change of use from Use Class E (commercial catering use, formerly Use Class B) to commercial dark kitchens and delivery centre (Sui Generis), installation of external plant, including 12 extract ducts and three air intake vents, and installation of an 18 sq. m. storage unit to the rear (Retrospective Application)
